content:
Write simple, executable Python code that follows the supplied contract exactly.

For parametrized tests, write complete explicit argument tuples; unpack them directly. Keep ordinary return-value cases separate from expected-exception cases. Do not build argument lists through conditional expressions or duplicate tuple elements implicitly.

Before returning a test file, check each case against its concrete argument values and required result or exception. For a reversed-bounds test, verify that the actual lower value exceeds the actual upper value. When isolating an invalid input, hold the other arguments valid. Match every parametrized name to a test argument; request fixtures only when they are supplied. Use the exact requested import.

Distinguish tests you inspected from tests you executed. State limitations precisely; do not claim completeness or that one exception-order case proves every validation ordering.

batches(items, capacity) accepts only exact built-in integers (reject bool and int subclasses). Validate both types before values. items must be >= 0 and capacity > 0, otherwise ValueError. Return the minimum number of capacity-sized batches needed for items; zero items needs zero batches.

Write one complete pytest file using the exact requested import. Do not implement, mock, inspect, or edit the function. No dependencies beyond pytest. Return one Python code block, then a short requirement-to-input mapping and accurate limitations. Do not claim execution unless you executed the tests. Do not claim exhaustive coverage.

strip_prefix(text, prefix) accepts only exact built-in strings (reject str subclasses). Validate both types before values. Empty prefix raises ValueError. Remove exactly one case-sensitive literal prefix if present at the start; otherwise return text unchanged. Empty text with nonempty prefix is valid. Whitespace and Unicode are ordinary literal characters.

Write one complete pytest file using the exact requested import. Do not implement, mock, inspect, or edit the function. No dependencies beyond pytest. Return one Python code block, then a short requirement-to-input mapping and accurate limitations. Do not claim execution unless you executed the tests. Do not claim exhaustive coverage.

Function contract: minute_of_day(text).

- text: an exact built-in str (reject subclasses).

Reject invalid specified types with TypeError before value/shape checks. All returned containers/scalars must have exact built-in types as described, recursively.

Accept exactly five ASCII characters HH:MM, hours 00..23 and minutes 00..59. Return hour*60+minute as an exact int. No trimming, signs, Unicode digits or extra characters. All malformed strings raise ValueError.

Do not mutate any input, including nested containers.

Write one complete pytest file importing 'from subject import minute_of_day'. Do not implement, replace, mock or inspect the function. Use only pytest and the standard library. Use explicit complete argument tuples. Return one Python code block, then a brief requirement-to-input mapping and honest finite-coverage limitations. Do not claim execution.
